stories.h: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer takes the widest UK release this weekend
stories.why: Weekend box-office watch with a big-name comeback
sum: Paramount is putting Ebenezer, Ti West's Dickens-inspired take on A Christmas Carol, into more cinemas than any other new title in the UK and Ireland this weekend. It marks Johnny Depp's first major US studio film in eight years, so its opening is being read as a test of whether his name still sells tickets.

Screen compares the launch against earlier Dickens adaptations and big franchise openers. Alongside it, Sony opens courtroom drama Prima Facie and heist comedy How To Rob A Bank, while Cristian Mungiu's Fjord arrives in a far smaller number of venues.
pts: Ebenezer is the widest new release in the UK and Ireland, at roughly 640 sites
It is Depp's first US studio film in eight years
Prima Facie, How To Rob A Bank and Fjord also open

stories.h: Fatherland leads European Film Awards nominations
stories.why: Early read on the arthouse awards race
sum: The European Film Academy revealed its 2026 nominees at the Thessaloniki festival. Pawel Pawlikowski's black-and-white Fatherland, about Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, leads with 11 nominations, including best film and director.

La Bola Negra, a queer love story spanning three eras of Spanish history, follows with 10, and Cristian Mungiu's Palme d'Or winner Fjord has five. Some festival favourites missed the main list. Around 5,700 Academy members voted, and winners will be announced at a ceremony in Athens on 16 January.
pts: Fatherland has 11 nominations, La Bola Negra 10, Fjord five
Hiam Abbass gets an honorary world cinema award
Ceremony takes place in Athens on 16 January

stories.h: Young crowds drive UK presales for You Can See Everything
stories.why: A documentary behaving like a event movie
sum: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's documentary about Elizabeth Holmes opens in UK cinemas through A24 on 20 November, in over 300 venues. Early ticket sales are strong, with some screenings selling out and extra shows being added.

What stands out is the audience: cinema chains report that people in their late teens to mid-thirties make up a large share of bookings, which is rare for a documentary. Online chatter is credited for the buzz, and the film has already grossed around $80m worldwide.
pts: UK release on 20 November via A24
Cineworld and Picturehouse report heavy presales from under-30s
Worldwide gross is about $80m

stories.h: IDFA opens with a plea for a gentler festival
stories.why: Documentary festival season kicks off
sum: At the opening gala of the 39th Amsterdam documentary festival, artistic director Isabel Arrate Fernandez asked audiences to slow down and step away from the constant stream of online content. She acknowledged that recent editions were shaped by disputes over Gaza and Ukraine, and argued that careful, empathetic storytelling can help people connect.

The night opened with the premiere of White Tiger Column. An anonymously funded 50,000 euro prize went to Sabine Groenewegen for The Clearing, a feminist look at abuses on Dutch colonial rubber plantations.
pts: Director calls for a calmer, more reflective festival
50,000 euro prize goes to The Clearing
DocLab marked its 20th anniversary with an audience game

stories.h: Being Heumann: warm, familiar disability-rights biopic
stories.why: True-story drama with a strong cast
sum: Siân Heder's film follows activist Judy Heumann, played by Ruth Madeley, as she fights in 1977 to get Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act enforced. A San Francisco protest becomes a sit-in, with Dylan O'Brien as a reporter and Mark Ruffalo as an official dodging her calls.

Little White Lies finds it likeable and uplifting, with a fiery lead performance and a strong disabled ensemble. But the reviewer calls it predictable and superficial, a feelgood triumph story whose political edge has been dulled.
pts: Ruth Madeley's lead performance is the highlight
Formula is safe and predictable
Praised for its disabled ensemble cast

stories.h: Fjord: Mungiu's Palme d'Or winner gets a savage pan
stories.why: Divisive awards-circuit arthouse title
sum: Cristian Mungiu's drama centres on a Romanian-born father and his Norwegian wife, whose strictly religious household is investigated by child welfare workers after bruises are noticed on their daughter.

Little White Lies is scathing. The reviewer argues the film seems keener to punish the parents than weigh the facts, paints the state as a witch-hunter, and leaves the children underwritten with a baffling subplot. It is a striking contrast with the film's festival reception and its European Film Awards nominations.
pts: Reviewer calls the film heavy-handed and one-sided
Child welfare investigator is portrayed as relentlessly hostile
Score of 1 out of 5 for enjoyment

stories.h: Prima Facie: Cynthia Erivo strong, film less so
stories.why: Stage-to-screen drama with a big lead
sum: The screen version of Suzie Miller's one-woman play stars Cynthia Erivo as Tessa, a defence barrister who cross-examines sexual assault complainants until she faces the justice system from the other side. The reviewer says the subject remains urgent.

Making Tessa a Black woman in a largely white profession adds a welcome layer, shown through her wigs. But the film loses the stage show's intensity, with plain direction, an overbearing score and a lead character who becomes a mouthpiece late on. Erivo is good, though poorly served.
pts: Erivo's performance is the best thing here
Adaptation loses the play's raw energy
Direction and score undercut emotional impact

stories.h: Nothing new from Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar today
stories.why: Checked every morning
sum: No releases, tour dates, features or announcements in the last 24 hours.

stories.h: Blackhaine's debut Saints in the Wethouse is a bleak, ambitious triumph
stories.why: Left-field, boundary-pushing sound beyond standard indie
sum: The Line of Best Fit's Tom Morgan reviews the debut full-length from Blackhaine, the Preston-born artist tied to Salford's White Hotel scene. He mixes futuristic rap with avant-garde ideas, including Butoh dance, to build a rain-soaked, nocturnal world of addiction and street violence that the review likens to the Red Riding novels.
The first half hits with abrasive club beats; the second turns more atmospheric before the closer drags you back into the dark. Morgan calls it visionary and electrifying, though also troubling.
pts: Debut album from a Salford-linked artist
Abrasive beats give way to atmosphere
Scored 9/10

stories.h: yeule shares Lovepill ahead of new EP a+e
stories.why: Experimental indie-pop with an alt edge
sum: yeule has put out Lovepill, the latest single from their EP a+e, due December 4 on Warner Records. The artist describes the project as a post-apocalyptic cyborg romance.

The track was written and produced with Deaton Chris Anthony, Devin Workman and Frank Dukes. Stereogum hears a deadpan, twisty dance-pop song with an electroclash feel. It follows lead single Hystérique, which the site picked as a favourite earlier.
pts: EP a+e arrives December 4
Co-produced with Frank Dukes and others
Electroclash-tinged dance-pop

stories.h: 54 Ultra's Honeymoon is a Clairo-produced shift into smoky pop
stories.why: Bedroom-indie lineage via Clairo
sum: New Jersey artist 54 Ultra (JohnAnthony Rodriguez) has released Honeymoon, co-written and produced with Clairo, Paul Cherry, Eddie Burns and William Corduroy.

It was recorded at Electric Lady Studios on analog tape with vintage gear, leaning on late-1970s smoky pop. Rodriguez bought a Yamaha CP70 piano just for the song and treats it as a new direction that still sounds like him. The page also lists tour dates across festivals, Europe and Australia.
pts: Co-produced by Clairo
Recorded to tape at Electric Lady
Tour dates listed

stories.h: Dicky Barrett appears to relaunch the Mighty Mighty Bosstones with a new band
stories.why: Alt-rock and ska-punk scene news
sum: Frontman Dicky Barrett looks to be reviving the Mighty Mighty Bosstones, who split in 2022 without explanation. They are billed to open Madness's Hollywood Bowl show on May 8, alongside Dance Hall Crashers, Goldfinger and Reel Big Fish.

An update says the set will feature Barrett with an entirely new backing band. Ex-Pietasters touring member Sammy Kay hinted on Instagram that original members aren't involved, calling it a hostile takeover. Barrett also has a pending trademark on the name.
pts: Bosstones set at Hollywood Bowl on May 8
Lineup appears to be Barrett plus new players
Original members' involvement disputed

stories.h: MALIQ & D'Essentials bring Rhoma Irama, Bilal Indrajaya and Perunggu on Kabar Gembira
stories.why: Indonesian scene, with Perunggu from the indie side
sum: MALIQ & D'Essentials released their tenth album, Kabar Gembira, on November 11 via Sony Music Indonesia. The nine-track set has three collaborations: Rhoma Irama on Penasaran, Bilal Indrajaya on Nyali, and the band Perunggu on Pigura.

Rhoma's link began with a song swap at Pestapora 2025 and he plays guitar on his track. Pigura was an older song reworked with new lyrics after talks with Perunggu. Arah Labuh came out as a single in October, and Life Is Madness is the focus track.
pts: Tenth album, out November 11
Features Rhoma Irama, Bilal Indrajaya, Perunggu
Focus track: Life Is Madness

stories.h: Avhath finally release a debut album after 14 years
stories.why: Heavier corner of the Indonesian scene
sum: Pophariini's Gerald Manuel reviews Avhath, the first full-length from an Indonesian band long known as one without an album. Its nine tracks arrive about 14 years after forming, produced by guitarist Rey.

Manuel is very positive, calling it a mature summary of their career that freshens their early sound with death-metal riffs and a playful streak. His pick is Cinereal Gaze, a slower and bleaker track. His one caveat is that the songs take many listens to stick and the fragmented arrangement may challenge newcomers.
pts: Debut album, nine tracks
Standout track: Cinereal Gaze
Slow-burn; needs repeat listens

stories.h: Melissa x Powerpuff Girls blind boxes
stories.why: Playful, candy-bright and collectible
sum: Brazilian jelly-shoe label Melissa has teamed up with The Powerpuff Girls for its first-ever blind box range. Each box holds a tiny figurine of Blossom, Bubbles or Buttercup, with a rare chase figure of the villain H.I.M. The figures are moulded in Melissa's vegan PVC and carry its fruity tutti-frutti scent.
The shoes are a low Kitten Heel thong sandal for adults, plus Mini Melissa styles for kids. It's on sale now at shopmelissa.com, and a candy-coloured installation is open at the Sao Paulo flagship.
pts: Blind-box figurines in scented PVC
Kitten Heel thong sandal for adults
Live now on Melissa's site

stories.h: Pokemon x Crocs clogs land 17 Nov
stories.why: Loud colour, casual and a bit silly
sum: Crocs is marking Pokemon's 30th anniversary with three clogs, each matched to a character's colour. Pikachu gets a yellow Classic Clog, Gengar a deep purple one, and Jigglypuff a pastel pink Classic Platform Clog.
They go on sale 17 November at Crocs.com. Japanese pricing is 13,200 yen for the Pikachu and Gengar pairs and 13,750 yen for the platform Jigglypuff.
pts: Release 17 November on Crocs.com
Yellow, purple and pastel pink
Jigglypuff is the platform version

stories.h: HERALBONY x ASICS GEL-1130 is out
stories.why: Artsy niche sneaker with colour pops
sum: ASICS SportStyle and the Japanese art label HERALBONY have turned the retro GEL-1130 runner into a canvas. The upper uses artwork by Michiko Koyama, known for dense drawings of tiny figures, on a paper-textured cream base.

Woven threads copy the pen strokes, with teal, red and orange accents on the toe, laces and heel. It costs 19,800 yen, roughly 124 dollars, and launched 13 November on the ASICS store, at a Tokyo pop-up and at Notre in Chicago.
pts: Artwork woven into a cream GEL-1130
About 124 dollars, out 13 Nov
Custom box printed with the art

stories.h: NOCTA Air Modmax in pink gradient
stories.why: A bold, colourful sneaker to watch
sum: New images show Drake's NOCTA line with Nike introducing the Air Modmax. The colourway, Pink Spell, has a pink gradient upper with volt, amber and cobalt touches, and three translucent amber pods in the heel.
It retails at 180 dollars and is slated for the end of 2026 on Nike.com. No exact date has been given yet.
pts: Pink Spell gradient colourway
180 dollars, holiday 2026
Debuts Nike's Air Modmax cushioning

stories.h: Tyler's Converse 1908 line is live
stories.why: Tomboy-friendly, colourful casual footwear
sum: Tyler, The Creator's GOLF le FLEUR* label has released a new Converse 1908 collection. The star is the Bronco Boot Low, a low-top take on last year's boot with suede and leather, a rubber toe cap, lugged sole and woven laces.

It comes in Cocoa Brown, New Wheat, Eden and Black. The Pro Leather returns in suede, and the Jogger arrives in High Risk Red and Golden Haze. It's available now on Converse.com, the GOLF le FLEUR* site and select shops.
pts: Bronco Boot Low in four colours
Pro Leather and Jogger also included
Available now

stories.h: Vans wrapped in Pringle argyle wool
stories.why: Preppy-meets-skate, easy to wear casual
sum: Vans and Pringle of Scotland have swapped canvas for brushed, felted argyle wool on three Premium shoes: the Authentic 44, Sk8-Hi Reissue 38 and Classic Slip-On 98.
Colourways are navy or black with white. The range also has cardigans, knit shorts, sweater vests, track sets, beanies and totes. Shoes cost 110 to 130 dollars and are on sale now at vans.com.
pts: Argyle wool on three Vans icons
110 to 130 dollars
Apparel and accessories too

stories.h: What London wore to silly, sexy Pouffe rave
stories.why: Playful, colourful, unfussy street style
sum: Pouffe is a new queer night in Tottenham, London, built around humour and maximalist colour. The second edition ran in November at Unit 58, with a large rainbow fuzzy mascot and a DJ booth dressed in hands and tentacles.

Looks ranged from sporty shorts and mesh or studded tops to vintage furs over printed silk slips. The founders enforce no dress code, just a loose brief of sexy and slightly silly. The piece has a 26-photo gallery.
pts: Humour and colour over cool
Sporty shorts, mesh, vintage fur
No dress code

stories.h: Eastern Indonesia coalition demands halt to nickel expansion
stories.why: Land and environment conflicts, civil liberties
sum: Ahead of COP31, a coalition of communities, Indigenous groups, women, youth and academics from Sulawesi, Maluku and Papua urged Jakarta to protect Indigenous land and forests and stop extractive expansion. They say eastern Indonesia is treated mainly as a place to exploit.

They cite a boom in captive coal plants serving nickel smelters, with Central Sulawesi capacity rising from 2.96 GW to 7.33 GW in two years, and about 81,000 respiratory infection cases in Morowali in 2025. They also report intimidation and criminalization of defenders.
pts: 99 of 411 nickel concessions reportedly overlap key biodiversity areas
Demands include revoking permits, auditing nickel zones and compensating residents
Coalition cites criminalization of environmental defenders

stories.h: Youth coalition calls Indonesia's energy transition a false solution
stories.why: Environment, protest and land conflicts
sum: Young activists and civil society groups marched in Jakarta on 30 October against continued fossil dependence; police blocked their route toward the Arjuna Wijaya statue. They argue B50 biodiesel, bioethanol, biomass co-firing and nickel downstreaming are false solutions that bring land grabs and ecological damage.

Government data cited show renewables at 17.3 percent of capacity while coal still supplies about 82 percent of the grid. The coalition also points to record fires and respiratory illness, and calls for a windfall profit tax on polluters.
pts: More than 2.8 million hectares burned through October, per Atlas Nusantara
401,586 acute respiratory infection cases recorded by the Health Ministry
Coalition wants a polluter-pays windfall tax

stories.h: Israeli strike in Khan Younis kills Hamas commander, hits displaced tent
stories.why: Major Gaza developments under the ceasefire
sum: Hamas confirmed that Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis died in an Israeli air strike in al-Mawasi, Khan Younis. Israel's military and the Shin Bet said they targeted a senior Hamas commander. Medical staff told Al Jazeera the strike hit a tent sheltering displaced people and wounded two others.
Gaza's Health Ministry says 16 people were killed in the previous 48 hours and at least 1,643 Palestinians since the October 2025 ceasefire. It also reports 11 cold-related deaths as winter sets in.
pts: Ministry figures: 1,643 killed since ceasefire began
Cold-related deaths reported at 11, including an infant
Israel's defence minister vows to continue offensive policy

stories.h: Israeli forces kill 14-year-old near Nablus as settler attacks mount
stories.why: West Bank violence and settler expansion
sum: Palestinian health officials say Israeli forces killed 14-year-old Moataz Iyad during an operation in Burqa, northwest of Nablus, and are holding his body. Wafa reported two other youths wounded and paramedics briefly detained. The Israeli military confirmed soldiers opened fire at a threat.
UN OCHA has documented more than 2,060 settler attacks causing casualties or damage across about 300 West Bank communities this year through 12 October.
pts: Wafa alleges ambulance access was blocked; Israel's account differs
OCHA: 2,060+ settler attacks since January
Gaza ministry: 1,613 killed since ceasefire (as of 10 Nov)

stories.h: Dockworkers strike across 100+ ports for Palestine; Cambridge votes to divest
stories.why: Antizionist and labor solidarity movements
sum: Mondoweiss reports strikes and actions at more than 100 ports in at least 22 countries demanding an end to the war on Gaza. Greek dockworker union leader Markos Bekris said workers hold power because weapons must be transported. The Palestinian labor movement has called a Day of Solidarity on 29 November.
Cambridge, Massachusetts voted 5-4 to divest from firms profiting from the occupation, while Providence voters weighed a binding divestment measure.
pts: Port actions in 22+ countries; only one East Coast US action
Cambridge pension reportedly holds about $18M in weapons makers
Solidarity day set for 29 November

stories.h: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections to September 2027
stories.why: Palestinian political representation
sum: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas decreed on 10 October that legislative and presidential elections due this month be pushed to September 2027, citing the need for national dialogue and participation from Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza, per WAFA.
Youth list head Fadi al-Sheikh Youssef called it unjust, while Hamas welcomed it as a step in the right direction. Analysts quoted say factions fear losing popularity.
pts: Hamas ready to join talks on reorganizing national councils
Critics say delay shuts out new political actors
Some displaced Gazans back it given conditions

stories.h: Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim elected to US Senate
stories.why: Muslim electoral win with Palestine stance
sum: An Al Jazeera opinion piece by Michigan Muslim American Bilal Irfan celebrates Abdul El-Sayed's statewide Senate win, the first for a Muslim in the chamber. Irfan argues it shows Muslims can enter public life without muting faith or Palestine solidarity.
El-Sayed ran on cost of living, healthcare and opposing the Gaza war, despite roughly $30 million spent against him in the primary by an AIPAC-affiliated super PAC, per the author.
pts: First Muslim elected to the US Senate
Campaign opposed the war in Gaza
Author notes one senator cannot end systemic problems
